title: A Prime Agent cannot operate without an Executor Accord and cannot amend the requirement away
content:
A.1.14.3.2 makes the pairing structural: "A fundamental requirement is that Prime Agents must partner with an Executor Agent. Prime Agents cannot be active without an active 'Executor Accord' which codifies their relationship with an Executor Agent. Prime Agents may not amend their Artifact or make any other procedural change that would have the effect of removing the Executor Agent Requirement." A.1.14.4.2 binds the other side: "An Executor Agent may not carry out any executive functions for a particular Prime Agent without a formal Executor Agent Accord."

The unamendability clause is drafted by *effect* — "would have the effect of removing" — so it catches indirect routes, not just a direct repeal. This mirrors A.1.14.1.6.2's protection of Sky Core's root control, and the parallel is instructive: both are structural dependencies that the dependent party is forbidden from engineering away.

The reason the dependency must be mandatory is that the Executor is not a service provider but a control. A.1.14.4.4.1 makes the Executor's alignment check on every Prime action unamendable, and A.1.14.4.5 gives it a right of refusal. An Agent that could shed its Executor would shed its compliance layer and its only operational route to the Protocol simultaneously.

The cost is a hard availability dependency: losing an Accord makes a Prime Agent inactive, not merely inconvenienced. That is precisely why A.1.14.5.2.1 forbids an Executor from completing termination "until all supervision arrangements are transferred smoothly to other Executor Agents" — the mandatory counterparty must be replaceable, or the requirement becomes a single point of failure for every Agent depending on it.
description: Partnering with an Executor Agent is a condition of being active, and any procedural change with the effect of removing that requirement is prohibited.
